text:
incident-bot: ALERT: queue_backlog.high for service=redis-backed-inference (region: us-west-2). backlog=3120 requests, avg_queue_latency=2.8s, autoscaler_throttle=TRUE. PagerDuty: PD-INC-4521 created and paging primary.

pagerduty: PD-INC-4521 — High backlog detected for redis-backed-inference. Paging on-call.

alice.m: I got the page, on it. Looking at metrics now. :eyes:

alice.m: Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ai/redis-backed-inference?panelId=7

benj: I see sustained enqueue rate ~1.2k r/s, processing throughput dropped to ~400 r/s after a kube node flapped. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up timeouts.

carlos: autoscaler controller logs show "scale request timed out: insufficient capacity in nodepool-gpu-usw2". Also EC2 spot pool had several terminations around the time.

alice.m: Ok — two vectors: (1) immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact, (2) root cause followup. For now let's try manual surge. @diane can you approve manual capacity increase for Dedicated burst?

diane: Approved. Triggering burst +4 g4dn nodes for pool nodepool-gpu-usw2. ETA 3-4m.

alice.m: While that spins up, I'm going to manually scale the inference-workers deployment replicas to 30 from 10 to push more pods onto existing nodes (temporary). Command:

```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-workers --replicas=30
```

benj: Logs show many pods stuck Pending due to nodeSelector: gpu=true. If new nodes don't come up quickly we need fallback: route low-priority traffic to cpu-quant model variant.

alice.m: Agreed. Starting routing policy change in Kong to shift weight 70/30 to cpu-quant for non-SLA customers.

```
curl -X POST https://kong.internal/routes/reconfig -d '{"service":"inference","weights":{"gpu":30,"cpu":70}}' | jq
```

carlos: I also pushed a temporary token bucket at the edge to throttle bursty clients: rate=500r/s, burst=1000 for anonymous keys.

pagerduty: PD-INC-4521 acknowledged by alice.m

alice.m: Manual scale hit some errors — see controller-events: "Insufficient vGPU capacity in AZ a". Burst nodes are provisioning in AZ b only. We need to ensure scheduler tolerates AZ spreading.

benj: I'm updating the deployment nodeAffinity to allow AZ b placement. Applying patch now.

```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment inference-workers --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":{"nodeSelectorTerms":[{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone","operator":"In","values":["us-west-2b"]}]}]}}}}}}'
```

alice.m: Patch applied. A few pending pods just moved to Running. throughput creeping up to ~900 r/s.

carlos: Queue length dropping to 1800. avg_queue_latency down to 1.5s. Good trend. Keep watching for regressions.

diane: Noted customer impact: several low-tier customers saw 5xx spikes and timeouts. Been triaging support tickets. Ops, please post template we can send to customers.

alice.m: Drafting quick customer note: "We're experiencing an autoscaling event caused by spot interruptions in us-west-2 which temporarily reduced GPU capacity. We've applied emergency burst capacity and routing changes; you may have seen elevated latencies or errors between 12:04-12:23 PDT. We're continuing remediation and will follow up with postmortem." Send to support? :thumbsup:

diane: :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PD-INC-4521 — Escalation to secondary in 8 minutes if not resolved.

oncall-rotations-bot: Handoff reminder — alice.m you will handoff to benj in 20m if incident persists.

alice.m: I'm continuing to monitor for 15 min. If queue < 500 and stable, we'll resolve and close PD. Refs: /var/logs/autoscaler/controller.log (tail):

```
2026-11-04T12:10:05Z autoscaler controller: requestedScale up x12 -> pending nodes 4
2026-11-04T12:12:18Z autoscaler controller: scaleTimeout. Reason: insufficient capacity in provider
2026-11-04T12:14:33Z nodeprovisioner: launched 4 instances in us-west-2b
```

benj: Noting follow-up items: (1) improve cross-AZ provisioning policy, (2) add fallback routing rules earlier in the autoscaler SLO path, (3) add per-model queue shedding for backpressure.

carlos: I'll open a provisioning playbook PR with exact steps to manually trigger Dedicated burst and to relax node affinity during emergencies.

alice.m: Queue is now 420, avg_latency 0.68s, error rate back to baseline. PD-INC-4521 resolving now.

pagerduty: PD-INC-4521 resolved by alice.m

alice.m: Quick post-incident notes posted to #incidents and I'll start the postmortem draft. Assigning action items: benj (autoscaler policy), carlos (provisioning playbook), diane (customer comms follow-up). Handoff to next oncall: @benj please take long-tail checks.

benj: Taking handoff. I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and follow up on tickets.

alice.m: Thanks team, great work. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
